nodes.description: The apical ectodermal ridge at the distal edge of the limb bud is the main site of Lrp4 expression. In Lrp4-deficient mice it forms abnormally from embryonic day 9.5, with ectopic expression and aberrant signaling of Fgf8, Shh, Bmp2, Bmp4 and Wnt7a and of the Wnt- and Bmp-responsive factors Lmx1b and Msx1, reduced apoptosis, and dorsal and ventral expansion of the ridge.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal development of the apical ectodermal ridge and polysyndactyly in Megf7-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: The reason for this developmental abnormality is apparent as early as embryonic day 9.5 when the apical ectodermal ridge (AER), the principal site of Megf7 expression at the distal edge of the embryonic limb bud, forms abnormally in the absence of Megf7.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal development of the apical ectodermal ridge and polysyndactyly in Megf7-deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: Ectopic expression and aberrant signaling of several molecules involved in limb patterning, including Fgf8, Shh, Bmp2, Bmp4 and Wnt7a, as well as the Wnt- and Bmp-responsive transcription factors Lmx1b and Msx1, result in reduced apoptosis and symmetrical dorsal and ventral expansions of the AER.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous germline LRP4 variants: mostly missense variants in the extracellular beta-propeller and LDL-receptor class B domains, plus splice, nonsense and frameshift alleles. The extracellular domain binds Wnt ligands; a beta1-propeller patient variant reduced Wnt11 binding.

nodes.description: LRP4 is the muscle receptor for neural agrin and activates MuSK to cluster acetylcholine receptors. The beta1-propeller p.Tyr607Cys protein reaches the plasma membrane and binds MuSK normally, but binds agrin and Wnt11 less, and agrin-induced MuSK phosphorylation is reduced. Patient myotubes formed fewer and smaller agrin- and Wnt11-induced acetylcholine receptor clusters. Most CLSS alleles have not been tested for this function and most patients have no neuromuscular symptoms.

LRP4 normally restrains LRP5/LRP6-dependent activation of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Patient missense proteins lose this activity in reporter assays, and several fail to reach the plasma membrane normally, consistent with misfolding of the extracellular domain. The result is excess canonical Wnt signaling in tissues where LRP4 acts, including the limb-bud ectoderm and the ureteric bud.
